findings.reason: The protected source is already the conventional optimal solution: sort once, fix each first position, and use two monotone pointers to count an entire valid right-endpoint block at once. Its first/left/right concepts are clear and the strict comparison and multiplicity are correct, so no candidate is justified.

The app-local and immutable Accepted native sources have identical in-place sort, fixed-position loop, pointer initialization, strict-sum branch, block-count update, pointer movement, and return behavior; only typing syntax and the required LeetCode class-method wrapper differ.

The original workload did not reject an $O(n^2 \log n)$ binary-search variant and a cubic control still passed at +0.13. Strengthened legal 16/64/192-value mixed-sign tiers remain within the -100 through 100 value and target bounds. The current source passes at +0.02 relative exponent with a 1.02x largest runtime ratio; a correct implementation with redundant whole-array work per pair passes every output and fails only scaling at +0.20.

The Approach proves why one successful pointer comparison counts a full block and why discarding a right endpoint is safe, accurately states Python sort workspace, and now labels strict inequality, duplicate multiplicity, and short arrays separately.

The hash-bound Premium Reference remains verified against the source structure, preserving all three factual examples, the first example's two qualifying triples, strict index ordering, and all five constraints.

coverage: all three source-fidelity-verified examples remain first and in source order as visible samples with exact inputs and outputs, including the formerly missing one-value example
